summary: A games room's shorthand stops becoming an arrangement: the note-candidates pass is now told which room it is reading, and an operator can say in policy.toml what kind of room it is.
details: The pass attributed every message to the WORKSPACE, not the room. On a workspace holding a Signal group, a WhatsApp group and a Discord games channel, every line of every batch read '(friends)' — the rooms were indistinguishable, and the renderer's own docstring had promised the room since the pass shipped. Each line now carries the room's own label from policy.toml ('Zone 42', 'Friends'), never a conversation id.

New optional `description` on a policy.toml conversation: one or two sentences saying what kind of room it is — 'a games room; 2200 is when people log on, not an appointment'. It is rendered once, verbatim, above the batch, as context for reading the messages and explicitly not as an instruction. Nothing can be derived from a room's own messages that says what the room is, so the operator is the only party who can state it.

What it cost before the fix: two notes, 'Bath gathering' and 'Bath gathering tonight', written from a fortnight of a games room's shorthand two days apart, the second one binding that day's '3 people' and '2200' onto a word that appeared nowhere in the batch.
The proactive pass's <home_room> block reads the same `description` field where one is set, so the two passes cannot hold two ideas of what a room is.
limitations: The `description` ships empty. It changes nothing on a deployment until the operator writes one per room; a room with none is described by nothing rather than by a guess.
A room the operator left unlabelled still falls back to its workspace name, which is the old behaviour for that room. The fallback is never the conversation id.

The <room> block renders on EVERY note-candidates prompt, described or not, so it is a prompt change for every existing eval case. The 20-case suite has not been re-run on this branch: two controlled cases (n10b/n11b — the incident's own batches, with the room described) are added so one live run answers whether the description changes the judgement, and no number from before this branch is comparable until it does.

`nora/dreamer/objectives/note-candidates.md` still tells the model it is reading 'a batch of messages from one group chat' and the notebook, and does not mention the new block. That file is `change_policy: operator-only`, so it is the operator's edit to make — and it is the half of this change most likely to decide whether the description is actually read.
